name: Postel's Law
description: Be liberal in what you accept from others, conservative in what you send — applied in UX to mean interfaces should tolerate messy user input while producing clean, predictable output.
design_relevance_note: Commonly cited for form-input tolerance and error-handling design.
myth_risk_note: Postel's Law (the Robustness Principle from RFC 761, 'be liberal in what you accept, conservative in what you send') is a named principle in network protocol design and software engineering, but no peer-reviewed empirical validation of this principle was found in the discovery data. Search results were contaminated by false matches on the technical term 'robustness'.
prevalence_note: Borrowed from networking's 'robustness principle'; its application to UX/design is a niche practitioner move rather than a mainstream design-curriculum reference.
